script: Return a wedding gift after 40 years. My aunt and her husband decided to divorce after almost 40 years. The paperwork was all good, no drama, just the usual "we're moving on" vibes. Then this ex‑uncle's sister slid into my aunt's DMs asking to return a coffee maker she'd bought them in '87. I was like, "Hold up, you want me to return a coffee maker?" (I know, right?) She said the coffee maker was dead and gone to the dump. She wanted a new one to replace it. "You want a new one for a dead old one?" I said, "That's the audacity, bruh." (Literally insane) My aunt hasn't responded yet. The family group chat is roasting her for the audacity. If I don't step in, she'll look like she's ignoring her own aunt, and the chat will keep laughing. The stakes? My aunt's reputation, the family drama, and a brand‑new coffee machine that might never actually get used. And here I am, waiting for the next roast to drop.
